author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A Microsoft Office application (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) started a command shell or script host. This usually means a malicious macro is executing.
false_positives: Office add-ins or business automation that legitimately launch scripts.
name: [WIN-001] Office application spawned a command or script interpreter
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the document that was opened and where it came from (email, download, share).
2. Review the child process command line for download cradles or encoded commands.
3. Isolate the host if the command line is malicious and scan it.
4. Check whether the same parent/child pair appeared on other hosts in the last 48 hours.
query: event.category: "process" and event.type: "start" and process.parent.name: ("WINWORD.EXE" or "EXCEL.EXE" or "POWERPNT.EXE" or "OUTLOOK.EXE") and process.name: ("cmd.exe" or "powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe" or "cscript.exe" or "wscript.exe" or "mshta.exe")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A web browser started a command shell or script host, which can indicate browser exploitation or execution of a downloaded payload.
false_positives: Developer tools or browser extensions that launch helper processes.
name: [WIN-002] Web browser spawned a command or script interpreter
note:
## Triage and response

1. Review browser history and recent downloads on the host.
2. Inspect installed extensions and remove unknown ones.
3. Patch the browser and run a full malware scan.
4. Look for the same behaviour on other endpoints.
query: event.category: "process" and event.type: "start" and process.parent.name: ("iexplore.exe" or "chrome.exe" or "firefox.exe" or "msedge.exe") and process.name: ("cmd.exe" or "powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe" or "cscript.exe" or "wscript.exe" or "mshta.exe")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: wscript.exe or cscript.exe started PowerShell, a common chain in script-based malware droppers.
false_positives: Legacy logon or administration scripts written in VBScript/JScript that call PowerShell.
name: [WIN-003] PowerShell started by Windows Script Host
note:
## Triage and response

1. Find the script file that was executed and review its content.
2. Review the PowerShell command line and any network connections it made.
3. If unexpected, isolate the host and collect the script for analysis.
query: event.category: "process" and event.type: "start" and process.parent.name: ("wscript.exe" or "cscript.exe") and process.name: ("powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: Access to the LSASS process memory or a known dumping technique (procdump against lsass, comsvcs.dll MiniDump) was observed.
false_positives: Security products and backup agents that read LSASS memory. Add them to the exclusion list.
name: [WIN-004] Possible LSASS credential dumping
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the process and user that accessed LSASS.
2. Treat credentials of every account logged on to the host as compromised; reset them.
3. Isolate the host and look for lateral movement from it.
query: (event.code: "4656" and winlog.event_data.ObjectName: *lsass.exe) or (event.code: "10" and winlog.event_data.TargetImage: *lsass.exe and not process.name: ("MsMpEng.exe" or "svchost.exe" or "wininit.exe" or "csrss.exe")) or (process.name: "procdump.exe" and process.command_line: *lsass*) or (process.name: "rundll32.exe" and process.command_line: *comsvcs.dll*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: Five or more failed Remote Desktop logons (logon type 10) from the same source address within ten minutes.
false_positives: A user repeatedly typing a wrong password, or a saved stale credential.
name: [WIN-005] RDP brute force from a single source
note:
## Triage and response

1. Check whether the source address is internal or internet-facing.
2. Look for a successful logon (4624) from the same source after the failures.
3. Block the source at the firewall and review account lockout policy.
query: event.code: "4625" and winlog.event_data.LogonType: "10"

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: fodhelper.exe was started by explorer.exe, a well-known technique to bypass User Account Control.
false_positives: A user opening "Manage optional features" from Settings, which also starts fodhelper.exe.
name: [WIN-006] UAC bypass through fodhelper.exe
note:
## Triage and response

1. Check HKCU\Software\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command for a planted command.
2. Review child processes of fodhelper.exe.
3. Isolate the host if an elevated shell was obtained.
query: event.category: "process" and event.type: "start" and process.parent.name: "explorer.exe" and process.name: "fodhelper.exe"

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: winlogon.exe started a command shell, which happens when an accessibility binary (sethc.exe, utilman.exe) was replaced to get a SYSTEM shell from the logon screen.
false_positives: None expected.
name: [WIN-007] Sticky Keys or accessibility feature backdoor
note:
## Triage and response

1. Verify the hashes of sethc.exe, utilman.exe, osk.exe and related binaries against known-good versions.
2. Check the Image File Execution Options debugger registry values for these binaries.
3. Isolate the host; treat it as fully compromised.
query: event.category: "process" and event.type: "start" and process.parent.name: "winlogon.exe" and process.name: ("cmd.exe" or "powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A value under a Run or RunOnce registry key was created or changed, a common persistence mechanism.
false_positives: Software installers and updaters that register themselves at startup.
name: [WIN-008] Registry Run key modified for persistence
note:
## Triage and response

1. Review the value name and the binary it points to.
2. Check the signature and reputation of that binary.
3. Remove the value and the binary if unauthorized.
query: (event.code: "4657" and winlog.event_data.ObjectName: *\\CurrentVersion\\Run*) or (event.code: "13" and registry.path: *\\CurrentVersion\\Run*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A process was started from a UNC path, which can indicate lateral movement or payload staging over SMB.
false_positives: Logon scripts and software deployed from NETLOGON/SYSVOL or internal file servers. Exclude those paths.
name: [WIN-009] Process executed from a network share
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the share and the account used to run the binary.
2. Review the binary on the share and who placed it there.
3. Look for the same binary executed on other hosts.
query: event.category: "process" and event.type: "start" and process.executable: \\\\*

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: PowerShell was started with an encoded command, often used to hide malicious scripts.
false_positives: Management tools (SCCM, monitoring agents) that pass scripts as encoded commands.
name: [WIN-010] PowerShell encoded command
note:
## Triage and response

1. Decode the Base64 payload (UTF-16LE) and review it.
2. Check the parent process and user.
3. Search for the same payload across hosts.
query: process.name: ("powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe") and process.command_line: (*-EncodedCommand* or *-enc\ * or *-ec\ *)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A new service was installed (System event 7045 or Security event 4697). Attackers use services for persistence and remote execution.
false_positives: Software installation and updates. Expect noise during patch windows.
name: [WIN-011] New Windows service installed
note:
## Triage and response

1. Review the service name, binary path and account.
2. Check the binary signature and location (services in user-writable paths are suspicious).
3. Correlate with software change records.
query: event.code: ("7045" or "4697")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A scheduled task was created (Security event 4698), which attackers use for persistence and delayed execution.
false_positives: Software installers and administrators creating maintenance tasks.
name: [WIN-012] Scheduled task created
note:
## Triage and response

1. Review the task XML (action, trigger, run-as account).
2. Check the referenced binary or script.
3. Delete the task if unauthorized and investigate the creator.
query: event.code: "4698"

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: PowerShell was used with a web download function, a typical way to fetch tools onto a compromised host.
false_positives: Administrative scripts that download installers from internal or vendor sites.
name: [WIN-013] PowerShell downloading content from the internet
note:
## Triage and response

1. Extract the URL from the command line and check its reputation.
2. Find the downloaded file on disk and analyse it.
3. Block the domain if malicious.
query: process.name: ("powershell.exe" or "pwsh.exe") and process.command_line: (*Invoke-WebRequest* or *iwr\ * or *Net.WebClient* or *DownloadString* or *DownloadFile* or *Start-BitsTransfer*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: wmic was used with "process call create", which can start processes on remote hosts.
false_positives: Administrative scripts using WMIC for remote management.
name: [WIN-014] WMIC remote process creation
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the target host (/node:) and the command started.
2. Check the account used and whether it is expected to administer that host.
3. Investigate the target host for follow-up activity.
query: process.name: "WMIC.exe" and process.command_line: (*process*call*create*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: sc.exe was used against a remote host (UNC name in the command line), a common lateral movement technique.
false_positives: Administrators managing services on remote servers.
name: [WIN-015] Remote service creation with sc.exe
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the remote host and the service binary.
2. Check the account used and the source host.
3. Investigate the remote host for the created service (event 7045).
query: process.name: "sc.exe" and process.command_line: *\\\\* and process.command_line: (*create* or *config* or *start*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: The Security log (event 1102) or another event log (System event 104) was cleared, often to hide attacker activity.
false_positives: Administrators clearing logs during troubleshooting (rare; should be documented).
name: [WIN-016] Windows event log cleared
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the account that cleared the log.
2. Review activity on the host shortly before the log was cleared using other sources (Sysmon, EDR, network).
3. Treat the host as suspicious until explained.
query: event.code: ("1102" or "104")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: Defender real-time protection was turned off or Defender settings were changed through PowerShell or Defender events.
false_positives: Approved exclusions added by administrators or deployment tools.
name: [WIN-017] Microsoft Defender protection disabled
note:
## Triage and response

1. Re-enable protection and check exclusions with Get-MpPreference.
2. Identify the account and process that made the change.
3. Run a full scan once protection is restored.
query: process.command_line: (*DisableRealtimeMonitoring* or *DisableBehaviorMonitoring* or *Add-MpPreference*-ExclusionPath*) or (event.provider: "Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender" and event.code: ("5001" or "5010" or "5012"))

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: The firewall logged traffic whose source address is in reserved or documentation ranges that should never appear as a source, which suggests spoofing.
false_positives: Misconfigured internal devices (for example APIPA addresses on a LAN interface).
name: [FW-001] Traffic from bogon or reserved source addresses
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the ingress interface or zone.
2. Confirm anti-spoofing / uRPF protection is enabled on internet-facing interfaces.

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: Twenty or more connections from the same source address were blocked by the firewall within one minute.
false_positives: Internet background noise against public addresses; vulnerability scanners you operate.
name: [FW-002] Many blocked connections from one source (possible port scan)
note:
## Triage and response

1. Check whether the source is internal (higher priority) or external.
2. For internal sources, identify the host and process generating the connections.
3. Consider blocking persistent external scanners.
query: event.action: ("deny" or "drop" or "block" or "reset-both" or "reset-client" or "reset-server")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: An internal host made an allowed connection to a destination located in a country on the watch list.
false_positives: Legitimate business with these regions, CDNs with mis-geolocated addresses. Adjust the country list to your policy.
name: [FW-003] Allowed outbound traffic to a high-risk country
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the internal host, process and destination service.
2. Check the destination address reputation.
3. Block the destination if the traffic has no business justification.
query: source.ip: ("10.0.0.0/8" or "172.16.0.0/12" or "192.168.0.0/16") and destination.geo.country_iso_code: ("KP" or "IR" or "SY" or "RU") and not event.action: ("deny" or "drop" or "block" or "reset-both" or "reset-client" or "reset-server")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: An internal host made an allowed connection to an internet address on SMB, RDP or WinRM ports, which should normally be blocked.
false_positives: Approved remote administration of cloud servers. Add their addresses to an exception list.
name: [FW-004] Allowed outbound SMB, RDP or WinRM to the internet
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the internal host and the destination.
2. Add an egress deny rule for these ports if one is missing.
3. Investigate the host if the connection was not expected.
query: destination.port: (445 or 3389 or 5985 or 5986) and source.ip: ("10.0.0.0/8" or "172.16.0.0/12" or "192.168.0.0/16") and not destination.ip: ("10.0.0.0/8" or "172.16.0.0/12" or "192.168.0.0/16") and not event.action: ("deny" or "drop" or "block" or "reset-both" or "reset-client" or "reset-server")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: Kaspersky Security Center reported a malicious or suspicious object, an object it could not disinfect, a virus outbreak or a network attack on a managed host.
false_positives: Test files (EICAR) and penetration tests.
Archives or installers flagged as potentially unwanted software.
name: [KAS-001] Kaspersky detected malware or a network attack
note:
## Triage and response

1. Read the detection in kaspersky.* (threat name, file path, action taken) and check whether Kaspersky removed the object.
2. If it was not cured or removed, isolate the host and run a full scan.
3. Find how the file arrived (download, mail attachment, removable media) and whether other hosts received it.
4. For network attacks, check the source address on the firewall and block it if it is external.
query: event.module: "kaspersky" and event.kind: "alert" and event.code: ("GNRL_EV_VIRUS_FOUND" or "GNRL_EV_SUSPICIOUS_OBJECT_FOUND" or "GNRL_EV_OBJECT_NOT_CURED" or "GNRL_EV_VIRUS_OUTBREAK" or "GNRL_EV_ATTACK_DETECTED")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: An HTTP POST request with a body larger than 1 MB was observed.
false_positives: File upload features of the application.
name: [WEB-001] Large HTTP POST request (possible exfiltration)
note:
## Triage and response

1. Identify the client and the endpoint receiving the upload.
2. Check whether the endpoint is expected to accept large uploads.
query: http.request.method: "POST" and http.request.body.bytes > 1000000

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A request carried a query parameter commonly used by web shells to run commands (cmd=, exec=, execute=).
false_positives: Applications that legitimately use these parameter names.
name: [WEB-002] Possible web shell command parameter
note:
## Triage and response

1. Find the requested file on the web server and review it.
2. Review other requests from the same client.
3. Remove the web shell and rotate credentials stored on the server.
query: url.query: (*cmd=* or *exec=* or *execute=*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A request targeted a file name commonly used for web shells.
false_positives: Scanners probing for these files (check the response status code).
name: [WEB-003] Request for a known web shell file name
note:
## Triage and response

1. Check the HTTP status; a 200 response means the file exists.
2. If present, isolate the server and review the file.
query: url.path: (*shell.jsp or *shell.aspx or *cmd.jsp or *cmd.aspx or *backdoor.php or *webshell.php or *c99.php or *r57.php)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A request used the user agent of a known scanning tool.
false_positives: Authorized scans by your own security team.
name: [WEB-004] Vulnerability scanner user agent
note:
## Triage and response

1. Confirm whether the scan was authorized.
2. Block the source if not.
query: user_agent.original: (*sqlmap* or *Nikto* or *nikto* or *Acunetix* or *DirBuster* or *Nuclei* or *nuclei* or *Nmap*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A request query string contained a typical SQL injection pattern.
false_positives: Search forms where users type SQL-like text.
name: [WEB-005] Possible SQL injection attempt
note:
## Triage and response

1. Review the response code and size for signs of success.
2. Check the application and database logs for errors around the same time.
3. Block the client and fix input validation.
query: url.query: (*UNION*SELECT* or *union*select* or *%27%20OR%20* or *%27%20or%20* or *SLEEP%28* or *sleep%28*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A request path contained a directory traversal sequence.
false_positives: Rare; some clients send relative paths.
name: [WEB-006] Path traversal attempt
note:
## Triage and response

1. Check the response status and size.
2. Review which file the request tried to reach.
query: url.original: (*../* or *..%2f* or *..%2F* or *%2e%2e%2f* or *%2E%2E%2F*)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: Ten or more 401/403/404/500 responses to the same client within one minute, typical of content discovery or brute force.
false_positives: Broken links, monitoring probes, misconfigured clients.
name: [WEB-007] Many HTTP errors from one client
note:
## Triage and response

1. Review the requested paths to tell scanning from broken links.
2. Rate-limit or block the client if scanning.
query: http.response.status_code: (401 or 403 or 404 or 500)

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: A request used a method that is rarely needed (TRACE, TRACK, DEBUG, PROPFIND, OPTIONS).
false_positives: CORS preflight requests use OPTIONS; WebDAV clients use PROPFIND.
name: [WEB-008] Unusual HTTP method
note:
## Triage and response

1. Disable unneeded methods on the web server.
query: http.request.method: ("OPTIONS" or "TRACE" or "TRACK" or "DEBUG" or "PROPFIND")

author: Elastic GenAI SecOps
description: Five or more failed logins (HTTP 401 on a login path) from the same client within five minutes.
false_positives: Users mistyping passwords; expired credentials in scripts.
name: [WEB-009] Web login brute force
note:
## Triage and response

1. Check for a successful login from the same client after the failures.
2. Enforce account lockout or rate limiting on the login endpoint.
query: url.path: *login* and http.response.status_code: 401
